primary.$description:
Purpose: The brand-gold fill for primary interactive action controls in their resting state.
Usage: Applied to primary button backgrounds and any control representing the most prominent call to action.
Guidelines: Use for the single most important action in a given context. Do not apply to multiple sibling actions of equal weight — reserve primary emphasis for one action per area.

primary-hover.$description:
Purpose: The darkened brand-gold fill for primary action controls on cursor hover.
Usage: Applied exclusively to primary button and primary interactive control backgrounds on :hover.
Guidelines: The perceptible shift from the resting state confirms interactivity. Ensure the change from colour/action/primary is visible but does not introduce confusion with a pressed state.

primary-pressed.$description:
Purpose: The deepest brand-gold fill for primary action controls in a pressed or active state.
Usage: Applied to primary button backgrounds on :active / pointer down.
Guidelines: Must be visually distinct from both the resting and hover states to provide clear interaction feedback. Do not use for non-interactive brand fills.

secondary.$description:
Purpose: The neutral fill for secondary action controls in their resting state.
Usage: Applied to secondary button backgrounds and any control presenting an alternative or supplementary action.
Guidelines: Secondary actions should never visually compete with a co-located primary action. Apply consistently to all secondary buttons across the UI.

secondary-hover.$description:
Purpose: A slightly darker neutral fill for secondary action controls on cursor hover.
Usage: Applied to secondary button and secondary control backgrounds on :hover.
Guidelines: The hover shift should be clearly distinguishable from the resting state without introducing confusion with the pressed state.

secondary-pressed.$description:
Purpose: The deepest neutral fill for secondary action controls in a pressed state.
Usage: Applied to secondary button and secondary control backgrounds on :active.
Guidelines: Must be visually distinct from hover. Maintain consistent pressed-state depth across all secondary interactive controls.

brand.$description:
Purpose: The primary brand-coloured surface; a gold fill for brand-forward components.
Usage: Applied to primary action surfaces, brand tiles, and any component where the full brand gold should fill the background.
Guidelines: Always use colour/onBackground/brand for foreground content on this surface. Validate contrast for all text and icon content placed on this background.

default.$description:
Purpose: The primary canvas background; the base surface of every page and layout.
Usage: Applied to the root body background, full-page layouts, and any area that represents the default visual plane of the UI.
Guidelines: Do not use for elevated or contained surfaces — use colour/background/surface or colour/background/raised instead. This token must always produce the highest (or lowest in dark mode) surface in the visual hierarchy.

error.$description:
Purpose: The background fill for error status surfaces, failure messages, and critical feedback containers.
Usage: Applied to error alert backgrounds, error badge fills, and any surface communicating a failed action, validation error, or critical system issue.
Guidelines: Always pair with colour/onBackground/error. Error backgrounds should appear infrequently and in response to genuine system or input errors only.

info.$description:
Purpose: The background fill for informational status surfaces, banners, and notification containers.
Usage: Applied to the container background of info alerts, info badges, and any UI surface communicating a neutral informational message.
Guidelines: Always pair with colour/onBackground/info for foreground content. Do not use for warning, error, or success states — each has its own background token.

inverse.$description:
Purpose: A dark, branded background for inverted UI regions where the surface adopts the brand's deep gold tone.
Usage: Applied to page headers, hero sections, promotional banners, or callout components that require a strong brand presence.
Guidelines: Always pair with colour/onBackground/inverse or colour/text/inverse for foreground content on this surface to ensure contrast. Do not use for large body content areas.

muted.$description:
Purpose: A clearly tinted background for suppressed or de-emphasised surface areas.
Usage: Used for disabled container backgrounds, inactive panel fills, or any surface that communicates reduced visual prominence.
Guidelines: Not for active, interactive surfaces. Ensure foreground content on muted backgrounds meets WCAG AA contrast requirements using the appropriate text token.

promo.$description:
Purpose: A deep gold promotional surface for high-impact, campaign-style UI regions.
Usage: Applied to promotional cards, marketing banners, and feature highlight sections requiring deeper brand emphasis than brand.
Guidelines: Use sparingly to preserve its visual impact. Always pair with colour/onBackground/promo for legible foreground content.

raised.$description:
Purpose: A background for elevated components that sit above the standard surface layer.
Usage: Applied to tooltips, floating menus, overlays, and components with a perceptible drop shadow that indicates elevation above sibling surfaces.
Guidelines: Reserve for components with visual elevation cues (shadow, border). Do not use in place of surface for flat components.

subtle.$description:
Purpose: A gently tinted background for page-level regions that need subtle visual separation from the default canvas.
Usage: Applied to secondary page areas, sidebar backgrounds, table row stripes, or any region-level tint that should not draw focus.
Guidelines: Shares the same primitive as colour/background/surface — differentiation in practice is achieved through borders and elevation. Do not rely on colour contrast alone to distinguish subtle regions.

success.$description:
Purpose: The background fill for success status surfaces, confirmations, and positive feedback containers.
Usage: Applied to success alert backgrounds, success badge fills, and any surface communicating a successfully completed action or positive system state.
Guidelines: Always pair with colour/onBackground/success. Do not use for neutral, error, or warning states.

surface.$description:
Purpose: The standard component background; the expected fill for contained UI surfaces such as cards, modals, and panels.
Usage: Applied to card backgrounds, dialog surfaces, dropdown panels, and any component-level container that sits above the default canvas.
Guidelines: Shares the same primitive as colour/background/subtle — border and elevation are the primary differentiators in practice. Use consistently across all card and panel components to maintain visual coherence.

warning.$description:
Purpose: The background fill for warning status surfaces and cautionary feedback containers.
Usage: Applied to warning alert backgrounds, warning badge fills, and any surface communicating a cautionary condition requiring user attention but not indicating failure.
Guidelines: Always pair with colour/onBackground/warning. Amber tones are inherently lower in contrast — verify all text on this surface meets 4.5:1 WCAG AA explicitly.

default.$description:
Purpose: The standard border colour for most contained UI elements and form controls.
Usage: Applied to input fields, dropdown containers, modal outlines, and standard component borders in a resting state.
Guidelines: Use as the default form control border. Always supplement with focus and error state tokens to communicate state changes clearly.

error.$description:
Purpose: The border colour for error status containers and invalid form fields.
Usage: Applied to error alert borders and input field borders in an invalid or error state.
Guidelines: Maintain 3:1 contrast against the error background and adjacent surfaces. This is the primary visual indicator of an error state on form controls — apply alongside an inline error message for accessibility.

info.$description:
Purpose: The border colour for info status containers, providing a visible boundary around informational feedback regions.
Usage: Applied to the border of info alert components and info-state input fields.
Guidelines: Maintain 3:1 contrast against both the info background and the adjacent page surface. Consistent use of status border tokens ensures users can identify status types at a glance.

interactive.$description:
Purpose: The brand-gold border colour signalling interactive focus and active selection states on form controls.
Usage: Applied to input field borders on :focus, selected control outlines, and any border communicating keyboard focus or active interaction.
Guidelines: Must always be applied to the focused state of all interactive inputs to satisfy WCAG 2.4.7 (Focus Visible). Verify 3:1 contrast against the input background surface.

strong.$description:
Purpose: A higher-contrast border for surfaces requiring emphatic separation or structural distinction.
Usage: Applied to strongly delineated sections, featured callout borders, and dividers requiring higher visual prominence than the default.
Guidelines: Reserve for contexts where colour/border/default provides insufficient visual separation. Do not use universally — overuse reduces the hierarchy of border emphasis.

subtle.$description:
Purpose: The lightest border colour for minimal structural separation between adjacent surfaces.
Usage: Applied to card borders, divider lines, and container outlines where a light, unobtrusive boundary is sufficient.
Guidelines: Ensure a minimum 3:1 contrast against both adjacent surfaces for non-text UI components. Prefer this token for containers that rely on background colour as the primary differentiator.

success.$description:
Purpose: The border colour for success status containers.
Usage: Applied to the border of success alert components and success-state input fields (e.g., after successful validation).
Guidelines: Maintain 3:1 contrast against the success background and the surrounding page surface. Apply consistently with other status border tokens for pattern recognition.

warning.$description:
Purpose: The border colour for warning status containers.
Usage: Applied to warning alert borders and any control border indicating a cautionary state.
Guidelines: Maintain 3:1 contrast against the warning background and surrounding page surface. Apply consistently with other status border tokens.

default.$description: Decorative-only. Standard divider for non-functional visual separations. Exempt from 3:1 contrast — use colour/border/default for functional boundaries.

strong.$description: Decorative-only. Most visible divider for emphatic aesthetic separation. Exempt from 3:1 contrast — use colour/border/strong for functional boundaries.

subtle.$description: Decorative-only. Lightest divider for table row stripes and aesthetic hairlines. Exempt from 3:1 contrast — MUST NOT be used for functional boundaries.

brand.$description:
Purpose: The brand gold colour for icons requiring brand expression.
Usage: Applied to featured brand icons, primary action icons, and interactive icons in brand-forward contexts.
Guidelines: Verify 3:1 contrast against the surface it appears on. Reserve for icons with intentional brand prominence — do not apply uniformly across all interactive icons.

default.$description:
Purpose: The standard colour for standalone icons in neutral, non-interactive contexts.
Usage: Applied to decorative icons, informational icons, and supporting visual elements adjacent to body text.
Guidelines: Verify 3:1 contrast against the background surface (WCAG AA for non-text elements). Do not use for icons that are the sole conveyor of information — supplement with labels.

error.$description:
Purpose: The colour for icons within error status components, typically a warning or cross glyph.
Usage: Applied to the leading icon in error alert and badge components.
Guidelines: Verify 3:1 contrast against colour/background/error. Reserve for error-status icon contexts only.

info.$description:
Purpose: The colour for icons within info status components, such as an information or notification glyph.
Usage: Applied to the leading icon in info alert and badge components.
Guidelines: Verify 3:1 contrast against colour/background/info. Do not repurpose this token for non-info-status icon contexts.

inverse.$description:
Purpose: A light icon colour for use on dark or branded backgrounds.
Usage: Applied to icons on colour/background/inverse, dark panels, and any dark-filled surface requiring light foreground icons.
Guidelines: Pair only with surfaces dark enough to maintain 3:1 contrast. Do not use on standard light backgrounds.

subtle.$description:
Purpose: A reduced-emphasis colour for secondary or supporting icons.
Usage: Applied to auxiliary icons, trailing decorative glyphs, and icons used in low-priority informational contexts.
Guidelines: Reserve for visual support roles. Do not use for icons that convey meaning independently of surrounding text.

success.$description:
Purpose: The colour for icons within success status components, typically a checkmark or confirmation glyph.
Usage: Applied to the leading icon in success alert and badge components.
Guidelines: Verify 3:1 contrast against colour/background/success. Do not use this token outside success-status contexts.

warning.$description:
Purpose: The colour for icons within warning status components, typically a caution or exclamation glyph.
Usage: Applied to the leading icon in warning alert and badge components.
Guidelines: Verify 3:1 contrast against colour/background/warning. Reserved for warning-status contexts only.

onBrand.$description: Button-safe text for brand surfaces. MUST NOT alias colour/text/*. White in both modes (primary action bg is dark in both). Verify 4.5:1 vs all action.primary states.

onNeutral.$description: Button-safe text for neutral surfaces. MUST NOT alias colour/text/*. Verify 4.5:1 vs all action.secondary states in both modes.

brand.$description:
Purpose: The foreground colour for content on brand-coloured surfaces.
Usage: Applied to text and icons within brand-filled components, such as primary button labels and brand tile content.
Guidelines: Always pair with colour/background/brand. Verify contrast at both light and dark mode values.

default.$description:
Purpose: The primary foreground colour for text and icons on the default background surface.
Usage: Applied to any text or icon element rendered directly on the default page canvas.
Guidelines: Use in combination with colour/background/default. Matches colour/text/primary in value — prefer colour/text/* for text-only contexts; use colour/onBackground/* when the token applies to both text and icons together.

error.$description:
Purpose: The foreground colour for text and icons on error status surfaces.
Usage: Applied to error message text, form validation labels, and icons within error alert and badge components.
Guidelines: Pair exclusively with colour/background/error. Verify WCAG AA contrast in both modes. Error text must be clearly legible — never compromise contrast on error states.

info.$description:
Purpose: The foreground colour for text and icons rendered on info status surfaces.
Usage: Applied to the body text, headings, and inline icons within info alert containers and badges.
Guidelines: Only use on colour/background/info surfaces. Verify WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 for text) against the paired background in both light and dark modes.

inverse.$description:
Purpose: The foreground colour for content rendered on inverse (dark branded) surfaces.
Usage: Applied to all text and icons on colour/background/inverse to ensure legibility on dark gold surfaces.
Guidelines: Always pair with colour/background/inverse. Do not use on standard or brand surfaces — each surface requires its own pairing.

muted.$description:
Purpose: A tertiary foreground colour for reduced-emphasis content on any background.
Usage: Applied to placeholder text, metadata, disabled foreground labels, and any content intentionally subordinated in the visual hierarchy.
Guidelines: Do not use for interactive or actionable content. Ensure the visual reduction in prominence is intentional and that the information is non-critical.

promo.$description:
Purpose: The foreground colour for content on promotional surfaces.
Usage: Applied to text and icons within deep gold promotional UI regions.
Guidelines: Always pair with colour/background/promo. Validate WCAG AA contrast for any text content placed on the promo surface.

subtle.$description:
Purpose: A secondary foreground colour for supporting text and icons on subtle or muted backgrounds.
Usage: Applied to supporting body copy, captions, and secondary icons on tinted or subtle page regions.
Guidelines: Verify WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 for text) against colour/background/subtle when applied. Do not use as the sole text colour for primary content.

success.$description:
Purpose: The foreground colour for text and icons on success status surfaces.
Usage: Applied to body text, headings, and icons within success alert and badge components.
Guidelines: Pair exclusively with colour/background/success. Verify WCAG AA contrast in both light and dark modes.

warning.$description:
Purpose: The foreground colour for text and icons on warning status surfaces.
Usage: Applied to warning message text and icons within warning alert and badge components.
Guidelines: Pair exclusively with colour/background/warning. Amber backgrounds make contrast compliance non-trivial — always validate 4.5:1 against this token's resolved value in both modes.

active.$description:
Purpose: A slightly stronger gold tint than selected, used for actively engaged or pressed interactive list items.
Usage: Applied to the active (momentarily pressed) state of list items, nav entries, or any surface showing a transient active interaction.
Guidelines: Distinct from selected in visual weight — active is transient; selected is persistent. Do not conflate the two in stateful UI components.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill for disabled interactive components; communicates unavailability.
Usage: Applied to the background of disabled buttons, disabled input fields, and any interactive control that is not currently operable.
Guidelines: Always accompany with colour/state/disabled/text for foreground content. Disabled states are exempt from WCAG contrast requirements but should still be clearly distinguishable from active states.

text.$description:
Purpose: The foreground text and label colour for disabled interactive components.
Usage: Applied to button labels, input text, and all text within disabled controls.
Guidelines: Pair with colour/state/disabled/bg. Disabled text is contrast-exempt under WCAG 1.4.3 but should remain perceptibly muted to communicate unavailability clearly.

focus.$description:
Purpose: The brand-gold colour used to render focus ring indicators on all interactive elements.
Usage: Applied to focus ring outlines (typically via outline or box-shadow) on buttons, inputs, links, and any focusable control.
Guidelines: Must be applied to all keyboard-navigable interactive elements to satisfy WCAG 2.4.7. The focus indicator must be clearly visible and must not be suppressed in any production context.

hover.$description:
Purpose: A subtle neutral overlay background applied on cursor hover to indicate that an element is interactive.
Usage: Applied to navigation items, list items, table rows, and any hover-sensitive container that does not use a dedicated action token.
Guidelines: Use as a lightweight hover signal where a full action colour is too heavy. Ensure hover overlays do not obscure underlying content or render adjacent text unreadable.

selected.$description:
Purpose: A soft gold-tinted background indicating a selected or chosen state on a list item, navigation entry, or toggle.
Usage: Applied to selected navigation items, selected list rows, and active tab or filter chip backgrounds.
Guidelines: Pair with colour/text/primary or colour/onBackground/default for foreground content — the selected state colour alone should not convey selection without additional visual cues such as an indicator.

inverse.$description:
Purpose: A light text colour for use on dark or branded surfaces where standard dark text would fail contrast.
Usage: Applied to text on colour/background/inverse, dark overlay surfaces, and any dark-filled container requiring light foreground text.
Guidelines: Only use on surfaces dark enough to maintain 4.5:1 contrast. Do not apply to standard light backgrounds.

link.$description:
Purpose: The standard colour for inline hyperlinks and interactive text elements.
Usage: Applied to anchor text, inline navigational links, and any text that initiates navigation or opens contextual content.
Guidelines: Ensure links are distinguishable from surrounding body text through underline or other non-colour cues, per WCAG 1.4.1. Verify 4.5:1 contrast on all background contexts.

link-hover.$description:
Purpose: The hover-state colour for inline links; communicates interactivity on cursor entry.
Usage: Applied exclusively as the link text colour on :hover and :focus states.
Guidelines: Maintain sufficient contrast from colour/text/link (resting) to communicate a visible state change. Also verify contrast against the background surface.

primary.$description:
Purpose: The default colour for all primary body text and high-emphasis typographic content.
Usage: Applied to headings, paragraph body copy, input field text, and any text requiring maximum legibility.
Guidelines: Use as the default text colour throughout. Ensure it maintains 4.5:1 contrast against all background contexts it appears on. Do not use for decorative or subordinate text.

secondary.$description:
Purpose: A reduced-emphasis text colour for supporting content and secondary labels.
Usage: Applied to subheadings, metadata, helper text, table secondary data, and any text that supports but does not replace primary content.
Guidelines: Verify WCAG AA contrast against the surface it appears on. Not suitable for critical user-facing content where maximum legibility is required.

tertiary.$description:
Purpose: The lowest-emphasis text colour for minimally significant labels and placeholder content.
Usage: Applied to input placeholder text, timestamp metadata, supplementary annotations, and visually subordinate labels.
Guidelines: Do not use for interactive text or content that conveys essential meaning. Placeholder usage should rely on other design cues to remain intelligible.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of error-status alert components.
Usage: Applied to the background of error alerts, destructive action warnings, and critical system failure banners.
Guidelines: References colour/background/error. Error alerts should be used only for genuine errors — overuse desensitises users to critical feedback.

border.$description:
Purpose: The border colour of error alert containers.
Usage: Applied to the border of error alert components.
Guidelines: References colour/border/error. Verify 3:1 contrast against surrounding page surfaces.

icon.$description:
Purpose: The icon colour for the leading glyph within error alert components.
Usage: Applied to the error icon (e.g., warning triangle or cross) within error alerts.
Guidelines: References colour/icon/error. Verify 3:1 contrast against alert/error/bg.

text.$description:
Purpose: The text colour for content within error alert components.
Usage: Applied to the error message text and any supporting labels within error alerts.
Guidelines: References colour/onBackground/error. Verify 4.5:1 contrast against alert/error/bg. Error message legibility is critical — never compromise contrast here.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of info-status alert components.
Usage: Applied to the container background of inline info alerts, banners, and notification toasts conveying informational messages.
Guidelines: References colour/background/info. Always combine with alert/info/text, alert/info/border, and alert/info/icon for a complete, accessible alert pattern.

border.$description:
Purpose: The border colour of info alert containers.
Usage: Applied to the left-accent border or full outline border of info alert components.
Guidelines: References colour/border/info. A left-accent border pattern is recommended for inline alerts — verify 3:1 contrast against the background behind the alert.

icon.$description:
Purpose: The icon colour for the leading status glyph within info alert components.
Usage: Applied to the info icon (e.g., info circle) at the start of the alert container.
Guidelines: References colour/icon/info. Verify 3:1 contrast against alert/info/bg.

text.$description:
Purpose: The text colour for body content within info alert components.
Usage: Applied to the message text, heading, and any inline links within an info alert.
Guidelines: References colour/onBackground/info. Verify 4.5:1 contrast against alert/info/bg in both modes.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of success-status alert components.
Usage: Applied to the background of success alerts and confirmation banners.
Guidelines: References colour/background/success. Apply with all four success alert tokens for a complete accessible pattern.

border.$description:
Purpose: The border colour of success alert containers.
Usage: Applied to the border of success alert components.
Guidelines: References colour/border/success. Verify 3:1 contrast against the page surface surrounding the alert.

icon.$description:
Purpose: The icon colour for the leading glyph within success alert components.
Usage: Applied to the success icon (e.g., checkmark) within alert containers.
Guidelines: References colour/icon/success. Verify 3:1 contrast against alert/success/bg.

text.$description:
Purpose: The text colour for body content within success alert components.
Usage: Applied to the message text within success alerts.
Guidelines: References colour/onBackground/success. Verify WCAG AA contrast against alert/success/bg.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of warning-status alert components.
Usage: Applied to the background of warning alerts and caution banners communicating non-critical but attention-requiring conditions.
Guidelines: References colour/background/warning. Pair with all four warning alert tokens. Amber-based warnings require explicit contrast verification.

border.$description:
Purpose: The border colour of warning alert containers.
Usage: Applied to the border of warning alert components.
Guidelines: References colour/border/warning. Verify 3:1 contrast against page surfaces adjacent to the alert.

icon.$description:
Purpose: The icon colour for the leading glyph within warning alert components.
Usage: Applied to the warning icon (e.g., exclamation mark) within warning alerts.
Guidelines: References colour/icon/warning. Verify 3:1 contrast against alert/warning/bg.

text.$description:
Purpose: The text colour for content within warning alert components.
Usage: Applied to the warning message text within alert containers.
Guidelines: References colour/onBackground/warning. Amber-toned warnings are prone to contrast failures — always validate 4.5:1 against alert/warning/bg explicitly.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of error-status badges.
Usage: Applied to badges communicating a failure, rejection, or error condition.
Guidelines: References colour/background/error. Pair with badge/error/text and badge/error/icon. Reserve for genuine error states.

icon.$description:
Purpose: The icon colour within error-status badges.
Usage: Applied to the leading icon (e.g., cross or warning) within error badge components.
Guidelines: References colour/icon/error. Verify 3:1 contrast against badge/error/bg.

text.$description:
Purpose: The text colour for error-status badge labels.
Usage: Applied to the label text of error badge components.
Guidelines: References colour/onBackground/error. Verify WCAG AA contrast against badge/error/bg.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of info-status badges.
Usage: Applied to the background of badge components communicating informational, neutral, or notification-type status.
Guidelines: References colour/background/info. Always pair with badge/info/text for legible foreground content. Use consistently with the alert info pattern for status coherence.

icon.$description:
Purpose: The icon colour within info-status badges.
Usage: Applied to any icon glyph (e.g., info circle) within info badge components.
Guidelines: References colour/icon/info. Verify 3:1 contrast against badge/info/bg.

text.$description:
Purpose: The text colour for labels within info-status badges.
Usage: Applied to the text label of info badge components.
Guidelines: References colour/onBackground/info. Verify 4.5:1 contrast against badge/info/bg in both modes.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of promotional badges used for marketing or feature-highlight callouts.
Usage: Applied to badges communicating a featured item, new release, sale, or promotional condition.
Guidelines: References colour/background/promo. Pair with badge/promo/text. Reserve for genuinely promotional contexts — do not use as a general-purpose accent colour.

text.$description:
Purpose: The text colour for promotional badge labels.
Usage: Applied to the label text of promo badge components.
Guidelines: References colour/onBackground/promo. Verify 4.5:1 contrast against badge/promo/bg.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of success-status badges.
Usage: Applied to badges communicating a successfully completed state, approved status, or positive condition.
Guidelines: References colour/background/success. Pair with badge/success/text and badge/success/icon.

icon.$description:
Purpose: The icon colour within success-status badges.
Usage: Applied to the leading icon (e.g., checkmark) within success badge components.
Guidelines: References colour/icon/success. Verify 3:1 contrast against badge/success/bg.

text.$description:
Purpose: The text colour for success-status badge labels.
Usage: Applied to the label text of success badge components.
Guidelines: References colour/onBackground/success. Verify WCAG AA contrast against badge/success/bg.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of warning-status badges.
Usage: Applied to badges communicating a cautionary condition or attention-required status.
Guidelines: References colour/background/warning. Pair with badge/warning/text. Amber tones require explicit contrast validation.

icon.$description:
Purpose: The icon colour within warning-status badges.
Usage: Applied to the leading icon (e.g., exclamation) within warning badge components.
Guidelines: References colour/icon/warning. Verify 3:1 contrast against badge/warning/bg.

text.$description:
Purpose: The text colour for warning-status badge labels.
Usage: Applied to the label text of warning badge components.
Guidelines: References colour/onBackground/warning. Validate 4.5:1 contrast against badge/warning/bg — amber pairings are susceptible to contrast failures.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of the primary button in its default resting state.
Usage: Applied to the background of all primary button instances across the UI.
Guidelines: References colour/action/primary — do not override this token with a raw primitive. Use button/primary/hover and button/primary/pressed for interactive state changes.

border.$description:
Purpose: The border colour of the primary button; set to transparent to produce a borderless filled button.
Usage: Applied to the border property of all primary button instances.
Guidelines: This token is transparent by design. Do not assign a visible border value unless introducing a distinct outlined primary variant — in that case, introduce a new token rather than modifying this one.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of the primary button when disabled.
Usage: Applied to the primary button background when the button's disabled attribute is set.
Guidelines: References colour/state/disabled/bg. Always apply in combination with button/primary/disabled/text. Do not apply hover or pressed state tokens to a disabled button.

border.$description: Primary button disabled border — matches colour/border/subtle. Apply the same logic as button/secondary/disabled/border.

text.$description:
Purpose: The label colour for a disabled primary button.
Usage: Applied to the primary button label text when the button's disabled attribute is set.
Guidelines: References colour/state/disabled/text. Ensure the disabled appearance is clearly distinguishable from the active state. No contrast compliance requirement under WCAG 1.4.3 for disabled components, but maintain perceptible muting.

focus.$description:
Purpose: The focus ring colour for the primary button.
Usage: Applied as an outline or box-shadow ring on :focus-visible to communicate keyboard focus on primary buttons.
Guidelines: References colour/state/focus. Must be applied to all keyboard-navigable primary buttons to satisfy WCAG 2.4.7. The focus indicator must be clearly visible and must not be suppressed in any production context.

focus-bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of the primary button in its focus state.
Usage: Applied to the primary button background on :focus-visible.
Guidelines: Aliases button/primary/bg — the background does not change on focus; the focus ring (button/primary/focus) communicates the focus state. Declared explicitly so the component token set is complete and the intent is unambiguous.

focus-text.$description:
Purpose: The label colour for the primary button in its focus state.
Usage: Applied to the primary button label text on :focus-visible.
Guidelines: White (#ffffff) in light mode — 5.43:1 contrast against gold/500, passes WCAG AA. Switches to neutral/900 (#1f343a) in dark mode — 6.31:1 contrast against gold/300, passes WCAG AA.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of the primary button on cursor hover.
Usage: Applied to the primary button background on :hover state.
Guidelines: References colour/action/primary/hover. Ensure a perceptible but not jarring visual change from the resting state.

Purpose: The background fill of the primary button in an actively pressed state.
Usage: Applied to the primary button background on :active / pointer-down.
Guidelines: References colour/action/primary/pressed. Must be visually distinct from both the resting and hover states.

text.$description: References colour/ink/onBrand — button-safe text decoupled from colour/text/*. Verify 4.5:1 against button/primary/bg at all states.

radius.$description:
Purpose: The corner radius applied to all button variants across all states.
Usage: Applied to all four corners of both primary and secondary button components.
Guidelines: Aliases radius/full (9999) — pill-shaped buttons. A single token governs all button states; corner radius does not vary between default, hover, focus, pressed, or disabled. To change button shape globally, update this token only.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of the secondary button in its default resting state.
Usage: Applied to the background of all secondary button instances.
Guidelines: References colour/action/secondary. Secondary buttons should co-exist visually alongside primary actions without competing for dominance.

border.$description:
Purpose: The border colour of the secondary button, providing visible delineation from the background.
Usage: Applied to the border of all secondary button instances.
Guidelines: References colour/border/default. Ensure the border provides at least 3:1 contrast against the page surface behind the button.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of the secondary button when disabled.
Usage: Applied to the secondary button background when disabled.
Guidelines: References colour/state/disabled/bg. Apply alongside button/secondary/disabled/text.

border.$description: Secondary button disabled border — matches colour/border/subtle. Apply the same logic as input/border/disabled.

text.$description:
Purpose: The label colour for a disabled secondary button.
Usage: Applied to secondary button label text when the button is disabled.
Guidelines: References colour/state/disabled/text. Maintain visible muting relative to the active secondary label.

focus.$description:
Purpose: The focus ring colour for the secondary button.
Usage: Applied as an outline or box-shadow ring on :focus-visible to communicate keyboard focus on secondary buttons.
Guidelines: References colour/state/focus. Must be applied to all keyboard-navigable secondary buttons to satisfy WCAG 2.4.7. The focus indicator must be clearly visible and must not be suppressed in any production context.

focus-bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of the secondary button in its focus state.
Usage: Applied to the secondary button background on :focus-visible.
Guidelines: Aliases button/secondary/bg — the background does not change on focus; the focus ring (button/secondary/focus) communicates the focus state. Declared explicitly so the component token set is complete and the intent is unambiguous.

focus-text.$description:
Purpose: The label colour for the secondary button in its focus state.
Usage: Applied to the secondary button label text on :focus-visible.
Guidelines: White (#ffffff) in light mode — 5.43:1 contrast against gold/500, passes WCAG AA. Switches to neutral/900 (#1f343a) in dark mode — 6.31:1 contrast against gold/300, passes WCAG AA.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of the secondary button on cursor hover.
Usage: Applied to the secondary button background on :hover.
Guidelines: References colour/action/secondary/hover. Ensure the hover state is perceptibly different from the resting state.

border.$description:
Purpose: The border colour of the secondary button on cursor hover.
Usage: Applied to the secondary button border on :hover.
Guidelines: Currently aliases button/secondary/border. Declared explicitly because secondary has a visible border — this token allows the hover border to be adjusted independently without creating a new token later.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of the secondary button in a pressed state.
Usage: Applied to the secondary button background on :active.
Guidelines: References colour/action/secondary/pressed. Must be distinct from both the resting and hover states.

border.$description:
Purpose: The border colour of the secondary button in a pressed state.
Usage: Applied to the secondary button border on :active.
Guidelines: Currently aliases button/secondary/border. Declared explicitly because secondary has a visible border — this token allows the pressed border to be adjusted independently without creating a new token later.

text.$description: References colour/ink/onNeutral — button-safe text decoupled from colour/text/*. Verify 4.5:1 against button/secondary/bg at all states.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of card components.
Usage: Applied to the background of all card variants — content cards, media cards, data summary cards.
Guidelines: References colour/background/surface. Cards should be visually lifted above the page canvas — combine with card/border and an optional elevation shadow.

border.$description:
Purpose: The border colour of card components, providing subtle visual containment.
Usage: Applied to the border of all card variants in their default state.
Guidelines: References colour/border/subtle. A light border is sufficient for most cards — avoid using stronger border tokens unless a card requires explicit callout emphasis.

meta.$description:
Purpose: The text colour for secondary metadata or supporting information within a card.
Usage: Applied to timestamps, author names, category labels, and any supporting text subordinate to the card title.
Guidelines: References colour/text/secondary. Verify WCAG AA contrast against card/bg for this reduced-emphasis text.

title.$description:
Purpose: The text colour for the primary title or heading within a card.
Usage: Applied to the card heading element (typically H3 or H4 typographically).
Guidelines: References colour/text/primary. Ensure title text maintains 4.5:1 contrast against card/bg.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of text input fields in their default resting state.
Usage: Applied to the background of all text inputs, textareas, and select components.
Guidelines: References colour/background/surface. Ensure input backgrounds are visually distinguishable from the surrounding page surface.

bg-disabled.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of a disabled input field.
Usage: Applied to the background of all inputs with the disabled attribute set.
Guidelines: References colour/state/disabled/bg. Apply alongside input/text/disabled to communicate a consistent disabled state across all input properties.

border.$description:
Purpose: The default border colour for input fields in a resting, unfocused state.
Usage: Applied to the border of all inputs, textareas, and select components when not focused, in error, or in success state.
Guidelines: References colour/border/default. This is the base state — always apply focus, error, and success border tokens as state overrides on top of this default.

border-disabled.$description:
Purpose: The border colour of a disabled input field.
Usage: Applied to the border of all inputs with the disabled attribute set.
Guidelines: References colour/border/subtle — a deliberately light border that recedes alongside the muted fill and text of the disabled state. Apply consistently with input/bg/disabled and input/text/disabled.

border-error.$description:
Purpose: The border colour indicating an invalid or error state on an input field.
Usage: Applied to the border of inputs that have failed validation.
Guidelines: References colour/border/error. Always accompany with an inline error message and input/text/error — do not rely on border colour alone to communicate the error.

border-focus.$description:
Purpose: The border colour for input fields when focused by keyboard or pointer.
Usage: Applied to the input border on :focus and :focus-visible states.
Guidelines: References colour/border/interactive. This token is required for WCAG 2.4.7 compliance. Must be clearly distinguishable from the default border colour.

border-success.$description:
Purpose: The border colour indicating a valid or successfully validated input field.
Usage: Applied to the border of inputs that have passed validation.
Guidelines: References colour/border/success. Use contextually — not all inputs require a success state, only those where confirmation of validity is meaningful to the user.

placeholder.$description:
Purpose: The text colour for placeholder content in input fields before user entry.
Usage: Applied to ::placeholder pseudo-element styling on all text inputs and textareas.
Guidelines: References colour/text/tertiary. Placeholder text is not a substitute for a visible label — always provide a label element in addition to placeholder content.

text.$description:
Purpose: The text colour for user-entered content within input fields.
Usage: Applied to the value text of all text inputs and textareas.
Guidelines: References colour/text/primary. Verify 4.5:1 contrast against input/bg at all input states.

text-disabled.$description:
Purpose: The text colour for content within a disabled input field.
Usage: Applied to the value text within disabled inputs.
Guidelines: References colour/state/disabled/text. Ensures the disabled input content is visually muted but still readable.

text-error.$description:
Purpose: The text colour for inline error messages and validation feedback associated with an input.
Usage: Applied to error label text, inline validation messages, and helper text in an error state below an input field.
Guidelines: References colour/onBackground/error. Verify 4.5:1 contrast against the page background it appears on.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of the navigation bar container.
Usage: Applied to the root background of the utility bar, main navigation bar, and any top-level navigation container.
Guidelines: References colour/background/default. Ensure the navigation background provides sufficient contrast from the page body below it; supplement with nav/border for explicit separation.

border.$description:
Purpose: The bottom border of the navigation bar, providing a subtle visual separation from page content.
Usage: Applied to the bottom border of the primary navigation container.
Guidelines: References colour/border/subtle. This token should produce a light, unobtrusive separator — avoid using a stronger border token here as it competes with content hierarchy.

indicator.$description:
Purpose: The brand-gold colour used to render the active state indicator on navigation items (e.g., underline or left border accent).
Usage: Applied to the active indicator element (border-bottom, left indicator bar) of the current navigation item.
Guidelines: References colour/action/primary. The indicator should always accompany nav/text/active — it must not be the sole means of communicating the active state.

bg.$description:
Purpose: The background fill of the currently active navigation item.
Usage: Applied to the background of the navigation item matching the current route.
Guidelines: References colour/state/selected. Use alongside nav/text/active and nav/indicator to create a compound active state with multiple visual cues.

Purpose: The background fill applied to navigation items on cursor hover.
Usage: Applied to the background of navigation list items and links on :hover.
Guidelines: References colour/state/hover. Ensure the hover background does not obscure nav/text readability. This token provides a gentle affordance signal without full action-level emphasis.

Purpose: The background fill of mega menu panels that expand from the primary navigation.
Usage: Applied to the background of dropdown mega menu containers.
Guidelines: References colour/background/surface. The mega menu background should sit clearly above the page canvas — supplement with nav/mega/border and an elevation shadow to establish depth.

border.$description:
Purpose: The border colour surrounding or underscoring the mega menu panel.
Usage: Applied to the border of mega menu containers.
Guidelines: References colour/border/subtle. Use to define the panel boundary without creating harsh visual separation.

title.$description:
Purpose: The text colour for section headings within mega menu panels.
Usage: Applied to category or grouping labels inside mega menu content areas.
Guidelines: References colour/text/tertiary. Section titles should be clearly subordinate to the menu item links — use as an organisational label, not as interactive content.

text.$description:
Purpose: The default text colour for navigation labels in an inactive, non-selected state.
Usage: Applied to all navigation item labels in their default resting state.
Guidelines: References colour/text/secondary. Verify WCAG AA contrast against nav/bg. Inactive labels should be clearly legible but visually subordinate to active navigation states.

text-active.$description:
Purpose: The text colour for the currently active or selected navigation item.
Usage: Applied to the label of the navigation item corresponding to the current page or section.
Guidelines: References colour/text/primary. Should be clearly distinguishable from nav/text to signal the active state — use in combination with nav/indicator for explicit active indication.

base.$description: Primary sans-serif (Jost) for UI text: labels, buttons, navigation, form elements. Site alias: --sans.

display.$description: Display serif (Cormorant Garamond) for display, headline and title roles. Site alias: --serif.

serif-body.$description: Serif (Lora) for body prose: paragraphs and running text. Site alias: --serif-body.

50.$description:
Purpose: The lightest step of the amber (warning) primitive scale.
Usage: Aliased into colour/background/warning in light mode.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Preserve pairing with amber/900 for dark-mode structural consistency.

100.$description:
Purpose: Second-lightest amber; a soft, warm-tinted surface value.
Usage: Available for aliasing into additional warning-status surface tokens if required.
Guidelines: Not currently mapped. Primitive-layer only.

200.$description:
Purpose: Third-step amber at a clearly visible warm tint.
Usage: Reserved for extended warning-status UI patterns.
Guidelines: Not for direct use.

300.$description:
Purpose: Mid-light amber primitive for visible warning borders.
Usage: Aliased into colour/border/warning in light mode.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Confirm 3:1 contrast against the warning background when applied via the semantic border token.

400.$description:
Purpose: Medium amber above the scale mid-point.
Usage: Aliased into colour/icon/warning in dark mode.
Guidelines: Not for direct use. Verify 3:1 icon contrast against the dark-mode warning background.

500.$description:
Purpose: Core mid-point of the amber scale; the primary warning amber.
Usage: Available for aliasing into prominent or interactive warning-status elements if required.
Guidelines: Not currently mapped. If aliased to text, verify WCAG AA compliance — amber hues are notoriously low-contrast on white.

600.$description:
Purpose: Dark-leaning amber with improved contrast on light warning surfaces.
Usage: Aliased into colour/icon/warning in light mode.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Confirm 3:1 icon contrast against colour/background/warning.

700.$description:
Purpose: Dark amber with strong contrast on light warning backgrounds.
Usage: Aliased into colour/onBackground/warning in light mode.
Guidelines: Not for direct use. Verify 4.5:1 contrast against the light-mode warning background. Amber can fail AA at lighter values — confirm explicitly.

800.$description:
Purpose: Very dark amber near the bottom of the scale.
Usage: Available for additional dark warning surfaces if required.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Not currently mapped.

900.$description:
Purpose: Darkest step of the amber scale.
Usage: Aliased into colour/background/warning in dark mode.
Guidelines: Not for direct use. Maintains structural pairing with amber/50 for cross-mode symmetry.

50.$description:
Purpose: The lightest step of the blue (info) primitive scale; a near-white blue tint.
Usage: Aliased into colour/background/info in light mode to produce a soft, legible info-status surface.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Paired with blue/900 as its dark-mode counterpart — do not mix primitives from different scales when aliasing status background tokens.

100.$description:
Purpose: A light blue primitive at the second step of the info scale.
Usage: Available for aliasing into light-tinted info UI surfaces if additional steps are required beyond the current semantic set.
Guidelines: Not currently referenced by any semantic token. Only alias if extending the info status palette.

200.$description:
Purpose: A medium-light blue primitive at the third step of the info scale.
Usage: Reserved for future aliasing; currently not mapped to any active semantic token.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Do not apply directly to component styles.

300.$description:
Purpose: A mid blue primitive with clearly visible saturation.
Usage: Aliased into colour/border/info in light mode to produce a visible info-status border.
Guidelines: Not for direct use. As a border colour, the resulting semantic token should maintain 3:1 contrast against adjacent info background surfaces.

400.$description:
Purpose: A medium-bright blue primitive sitting above the scale mid-point.
Usage: Aliased into colour/icon/info in dark mode.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Verify icon contrast meets 3:1 against the dark-mode info background when aliased.

500.$description:
Purpose: The core mid-point of the blue scale; the primary reference blue.
Usage: Available for aliasing into interactive info-status elements if needed beyond current semantic coverage.
Guidelines: Not currently mapped to an active semantic token. If aliased to a text token, verify WCAG AA compliance.

600.$description:
Purpose: A dark-leaning blue providing strong contrast against light info surfaces.
Usage: Aliased into colour/icon/info in light mode.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Confirm icon contrast (3:1 minimum) against colour/background/info when the semantic token is applied.

700.$description:
Purpose: A dark blue with high contrast against the lightest info backgrounds.
Usage: Aliased into colour/onBackground/info in light mode for legible text and foreground content on info surfaces.
Guidelines: Not for direct use. When aliased to onBackground tokens, verify 4.5:1 contrast against the paired info background primitive.

800.$description:
Purpose: A very dark blue near the base of the scale.
Usage: Available for deep dark-mode info backgrounds or additional aliasing if required.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Currently not mapped. Alias only if extending the info status colour depth.

900.$description:
Purpose: The darkest step of the blue scale; a near-black deep blue.
Usage: Aliased into colour/background/info in dark mode.
Guidelines: Not for direct use. Paired with blue/50 as the light-mode counterpart — maintains structural symmetry across the status scale.

25.$description:
Purpose: The lightest step in the gold primitive scale; a near-white tinted surface value.
Usage: Referenced by semantic tokens requiring a very subtle gold-tinted wash, such as colour/state/selected in light mode.
Guidelines: Do not apply directly to component design. All usage must flow through a semantic alias. Reserve for contexts where the tint is barely perceptible against a white background.

50.$description:
Purpose: A soft, low-saturation gold primitive establishing the second lightest step in the scale.
Usage: Consumed by semantic tokens that require a light gold background, such as state and hover overlays.
Guidelines: Not for direct use in layouts or components. Should always be aliased through a semantic token.

100.$description:
Purpose: A light gold primitive representing the third step of the scale.
Usage: Available for aliasing into semantic tokens where a light but visible gold fill is required.
Guidelines: Use only as a primitive source value. Do not hard-code into component styles.

200.$description:
Purpose: A medium-light gold primitive at the fourth step of the scale.
Usage: Provides a mid-range light value for gold; usable as a source for subtle border or tinted fill tokens.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Must be consumed via a semantic token alias.

300.$description:
Purpose: A mid-range gold primitive establishing a clearly visible, unsaturated gold.
Usage: Aliased into semantic tokens for interactive borders, icon fills, and link text in dark mode contexts.
Guidelines: Not for direct application. Check contrast ratio when aliasing to text or icon tokens — minimum 4.5:1 required for WCAG AA compliance.

400.$description:
Purpose: A medium gold primitive at the fifth-brightest step of the scale.
Usage: Source value for semantic action, icon, and interactive element tokens in dark mode.
Guidelines: Validate contrast when used as foreground on dark surfaces. Not for direct use in component design.

500.$description:
Purpose: The core brand gold; the primary mid-point of the scale and the anchor for the brand identity.
Usage: Aliased into colour/action/primary (light mode) and colour/background/brand. The single brand-colour source value provided by the brand designer.
Guidelines: Treat as the canonical brand colour. When aliasing to text or icon contexts, verify WCAG AA compliance. Do not substitute other primitives where gold/500 is expected.

600.$description:
Purpose: A darkened brand gold primitive one step below the mid-point.
Usage: Aliased into hover state tokens for primary actions in light mode (colour/action/primary/hover).
Guidelines: Use to communicate interaction depth on primary actions. Maintain at least one step of contrast against the resting-state primitive.

700.$description:
Purpose: A dark gold primitive providing strong contrast against light surfaces.
Usage: Aliased into pressed/active state tokens for primary actions in light mode, and into colour/background/promo.
Guidelines: Reserved for pressed states and promotional backgrounds. Do not use where a softer brand presence is required.

800.$description:
Purpose: A very dark gold primitive approaching near-black saturation.
Usage: Available for aliasing into dark, high-contrast gold surfaces such as deep brand backgrounds.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Ensure any foreground aliased against this value meets 4.5:1 contrast for text.

900.$description:
Purpose: The darkest gold near the bottom of the scale, suitable for deep inverse backgrounds.
Usage: Aliased into colour/background/inverse to provide the dark branded surface in light mode.
Guidelines: Only use in contexts where maximum gold depth is required. Foreground on this surface must be a near-white neutral.

950.$description:
Purpose: The absolute darkest step of the gold scale; near-black with a gold undertone.
Usage: Available as a source value for the very deepest gold surfaces if required by future component needs.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Use sparingly — prefer gold/900 unless maximum depth is explicitly required.

50.$description:
Purpose: The lightest step of the green (success) primitive scale.
Usage: Aliased into colour/background/success in light mode.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Preserve the structural pairing with green/900 for dark-mode aliasing.

100.$description:
Purpose: Second-lightest green primitive; a light tinted green surface value.
Usage: Available for aliasing into additional success-status surface tokens if required.
Guidelines: Not currently mapped to an active semantic token. Primitive-layer only.

200.$description:
Purpose: Third-step green primitive at a clearly visible light tint.
Usage: Reserved for future aliasing or extended success-status UI patterns.
Guidelines: Not for direct use. Only alias if extending the success palette beyond current semantic coverage.

300.$description:
Purpose: Mid-light green primitive providing a visible, saturated border value.
Usage: Aliased into colour/border/success in light mode.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Confirm 3:1 contrast against success background when applied via the border semantic token.

400.$description:
Purpose: Medium green primitive above the mid-point of the success scale.
Usage: Aliased into colour/icon/success in dark mode.
Guidelines: Not for direct use. Verify icon contrast (3:1 minimum) against the dark-mode success background.

500.$description:
Purpose: Core mid-point of the green scale; the primary success green.
Usage: Available for aliasing into interactive or prominent success-status UI elements.
Guidelines: Not currently mapped to an active semantic token. If aliased to text, verify WCAG AA compliance.

600.$description:
Purpose: Dark-leaning green providing strong contrast on light success surfaces.
Usage: Aliased into colour/icon/success in light mode.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Confirm 3:1 icon contrast against colour/background/success when applied.

700.$description:
Purpose: Dark green with high legibility on light success backgrounds.
Usage: Aliased into colour/onBackground/success in light mode for text and foreground content on success surfaces.
Guidelines: Not for direct use. Verify 4.5:1 contrast against the light-mode success background.

800.$description:
Purpose: Very dark green near the bottom of the scale.
Usage: Available for deeper dark-mode or high-contrast success surfaces if required.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Not currently mapped. Only alias if extending the success palette.

900.$description:
Purpose: Darkest step of the green scale; near-black with a green undertone.
Usage: Aliased into colour/background/success in dark mode.
Guidelines: Not for direct use. Maintains structural pairing with green/50 for cross-mode symmetry.

0.$description:
Purpose: The zero-point anchor of the neutral scale; pure white in light mode and the deepest dark-mode base in dark mode.
Usage: Aliased into colour/background/default and colour/background/raised in light mode; inverted to the darkest surface in dark mode.
Guidelines: A special-case primitive. Never substitute another step where neutral/0 is expected, as it carries structural meaning as both the lightest and darkest extremes depending on mode.

50.$description:
Purpose: The lightest non-white step of the neutral scale; a very subtle off-white.
Usage: Aliased into colour/background/subtle and colour/background/surface to distinguish page-level tinted regions and component backgrounds from the default canvas.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Note that subtle and surface share this primitive intentionally — semantic differentiation is achieved through borders and elevation, not colour alone.

100.$description:
Purpose: A light neutral primitive providing a soft, visible background distinction.
Usage: Aliased into colour/background/muted, colour/border/subtle, and colour/state/disabled/bg.
Guidelines: Not for direct use. When aliased to border tokens, ensure visual separation from adjacent surfaces is sufficient without relying on this colour alone.

200.$description:
Purpose: A slightly darker light neutral, providing a clearly visible but low-contrast value.
Usage: Aliased into colour/border/default and colour/action/secondary for default borders and secondary action fills.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Border tokens aliasing this value must maintain a minimum 3:1 contrast ratio against adjacent surfaces per WCAG AA.

300.$description:
Purpose: A mid-light neutral sitting at a clearly visible step between light and mid tones.
Usage: Aliased into colour/border/strong and colour/action/secondary/hover.
Guidelines: Not for direct use. When aliased to interactive controls, verify that hover states provide sufficient visual change from the resting state.

400.$description:
Purpose: A mid neutral at the boundary between light and medium tones.
Usage: Aliased into colour/text/tertiary (light mode), colour/state/disabled/text, and colour/action/secondary/pressed.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. When aliased to text tokens, ensure the resulting combination meets WCAG AA contrast against its background context.

500.$description:
Purpose: The true mid-point of the neutral scale; a balanced grey with equal contrast in both directions.
Usage: Aliased into colour/text/secondary (light mode) and colour/onBackground/muted in light mode.
Guidelines: Not for direct use. The mirror relationship between neutral/500 and neutral/400 across modes is intentional — validate both mode outputs when modifying this token.

600.$description:
Purpose: A mid-dark neutral providing stronger contrast than the mid-point.
Usage: Aliased into colour/text/secondary (light mode) and colour/onBackground/subtle in light mode.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Confirm WCAG AA compliance (4.5:1 for body text) against all background contexts where this value is applied via semantic aliases.

700.$description:
Purpose: A dark neutral close to the deep anchor, suitable for icon and secondary heading values.
Usage: Aliased into colour/icon/default to ensure icons read clearly against light surfaces.
Guidelines: Not for direct use. As an icon colour source, the semantic token should maintain 3:1 contrast against the surface it appears on.

800.$description:
Purpose: A very dark neutral near the bottom of the light-mode scale.
Usage: Aliased into component-layer tokens and dark-mode background tokens requiring high-contrast dark fills.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Use to support elevation distinctions in dark mode through subtle tonal differences.

900.$description:
Purpose: The near-darkest neutral in the scale; a deep, ink-like tone for primary text and strong foreground elements.
Usage: Aliased into colour/text/primary and colour/onBackground/default in light mode.
Guidelines: Not for direct use. Always verify 7:1 contrast against the default background for AAA compliance, and minimum 4.5:1 for AA.

950.$description:
Purpose: The darkest step in the neutral scale; the primary dark-mode base surface colour.
Usage: Aliased into colour/background/default in dark mode and colour/text/inverse in light mode.
Guidelines: A structural anchor primitive. Changes to this value propagate broadly — always audit all downstream semantic aliases before modifying.

50.$description:
Purpose: The lightest step of the red (error) primitive scale.
Usage: Aliased into colour/background/error in light mode.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Preserve the structural pairing with red/900 for dark-mode aliasing consistency.

100.$description:
Purpose: Second-lightest red; a soft, low-saturation error-tinted surface.
Usage: Available for aliasing into additional error-status surface tokens if required.
Guidelines: Not currently mapped. Primitive-layer only.

200.$description:
Purpose: Third-step red primitive at a clearly visible light tint.
Usage: Reserved for future aliasing or extended error-status UI patterns.
Guidelines: Not for direct use.

300.$description:
Purpose: Mid-light red primitive for visible error-status borders.
Usage: Aliased into colour/border/error in light mode.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Ensure 3:1 contrast against the error background when applied via the semantic border token.

400.$description:
Purpose: Medium red above the scale mid-point.
Usage: Aliased into colour/icon/error in dark mode.
Guidelines: Not for direct use. Verify 3:1 icon contrast against the dark-mode error background.

500.$description:
Purpose: Core mid-point of the red scale; the primary error red.
Usage: Available for aliasing into prominent or interactive error-status UI elements if required.
Guidelines: Not currently mapped. If aliased to text, verify WCAG AA compliance.

600.$description:
Purpose: Dark-leaning red with high contrast on light error surfaces.
Usage: Aliased into colour/icon/error in light mode.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Confirm 3:1 icon contrast against colour/background/error.

700.$description:
Purpose: Dark red with strong contrast on light error backgrounds.
Usage: Aliased into colour/onBackground/error in light mode.
Guidelines: Not for direct use. Verify 4.5:1 contrast against the light-mode error background.

800.$description:
Purpose: Very dark red near the bottom of the scale.
Usage: Available for additional dark error surfaces if required.
Guidelines: Primitive-layer only. Not currently mapped.

900.$description:
Purpose: Darkest step of the red scale; near-black with a red undertone.
Usage: Aliased into colour/background/error in dark mode.
Guidelines: Not for direct use. Maintains structural pairing with red/50 for cross-mode symmetry.

transparent.$description:
Purpose: A fully transparent colour primitive; the zero-alpha anchor of the colour system.
Usage: Referenced by any token that requires a genuinely invisible fill or border — e.g. button/primary/border where no visible border is desired.
Guidelines: Do not substitute with a colour-matched value (e.g. same colour as bg) when true transparency is the intent. Changes to this value would propagate broadly — treat as immutable.
